response: Yes, the Mammography Quality Standards Act (MQSA) has had a positive impact on mammography quality in North Carolina. The MQSA, enacted in 1992, established national quality standards for mammography facilities, including requirements for equipment, personnel, and quality control. As a result, mammography facilities in North Carolina, like those across the US, have had to meet these standards, leading to improved image quality, reduced radiation doses, and enhanced patient care. Regular inspections and accreditation by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) or state-certified accrediting bodies have helped ensure compliance with these standards, ultimately contributing to better mammography quality in North Carolina.
